headline: Federal government rejects local bid for Montpelier post office site
dek: The General Services Administration plans to reopen bidding for the flood-damaged former post office after turning down a $540,000 offer from a local redevelopment group.
body: The federal government has rejected a local group’s bid to buy Montpelier’s former post office, keeping the flood-damaged property on the market while officials prepare to reopen the auction, Vermont Public reported Monday.

The 87 State Street Local Development Corporation offered $540,000 for the building after placing the highest bid in an August auction. The General Services Administration said the offer was below the property’s value, according to the report. The site’s original asking price was $2.4 million.

The group formed to help redevelop the property after the post office moved following the 2023 flood. Its proposed plans are complicated by environmental testing that found widespread PCB contamination and by the building’s location in the Winooski River floodplain. The local group says cleanup could cost as much as $3 million.

The decision prolongs uncertainty around a prominent downtown property that local officials and redevelopment advocates had hoped could support new housing and office space. The development corporation said it will continue pursuing the building when the federal auction is reopened.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Federal government rejects local bid for Montpelier post office site
seoDescription: The GSA will reopen bidding for Montpelier’s flood-damaged former post office after rejecting a $540,000 local redevelopment bid.
